title: Continuo: the walk, tick by tick
representation: A 2x2 square of the four modes the bot can be in (walking or not, searching or not), with the jobs done in each mode, the transitions and endings between them, the doors to the game on the right, the keys on the left, the order of one tick below and the build plan above. Four lenses over the same picture: what happens, what can be tuned, how sure we are, what must hold.

kinds.standby: A state outside a loaded world
kinds.guard: The shared gatekeeper around the bot
kinds.mode: One of the four modes the bot can be in
kinds.job: A job done while in a mode
kinds.outcome: A way a walk ends, with its log line
kinds.door: One of the five openings between bot and game
kinds.version: A game the bot is plugged into
kinds.beat: A step that happens, in order, every tick
kinds.milestone: A stage of the build plan
kinds.dial: A number or switch that changes behaviour

proofLevels.game: Seen working in a real game, recorded in the repo
proofLevels.tests: Automated tests only; no in-game record
proofLevels.reasoned: Reasoned or extrapolated; not measured or not tested

elements.name: Mark this spot
elements.summary: Remembers the block you are standing on as the goal; a new press replaces the old mark.
facts: Logs "Continuo: path goal marked at x y z"
The mark is forgotten when the world or dimension changes
There is no other way to name a destination yet
elements.evidence: In-game run 2026-09-02: the route test turned the player toward the marked goal on both versions.

elements.name: Walk to the mark
elements.summary: Starts a walk to the marked block, replacing any walk already in progress.
facts: Pressed with nothing marked: logs a hint and does nothing
Presses made outside a world are thrown away
This key is the only way to start the bot today
log: Continuo: no goal marked -- stand on the destination and press the mark key
elements.evidence: The key itself was exercised in game through 2026-09-02, but then it drove a 40-tick straight walk. No run is recorded since it was rewired to the route walker.

elements.name: Test a route
elements.summary: Developer key: searches for a route to the mark without walking it, and writes a report.
facts: Pressing it mid-walk is expected to produce spurious notices

elements.name: Dump a block row
elements.summary: Developer key: writes how the bot sees the 32 blocks east of you to a text file.

elements.name: Route test report
elements.summary: Runs the route search on the live world three times, times it, draws the route as a text map and checks the player readings.
facts: Writes continuo-path-probe.txt in the game folder
Allows gap jumps, unlike a real walk
Runs twice more on a frozen copy to separate reading cost from thinking cost
Warns if "on ground" disagrees with the block under the feet
Warns if the view did not turn as asked
log: Continuo path probe: FOUND, 2 segments, 245 steps, 25053 expanded, cost ...
Continuo: wrote path probe map to <path>
gaps: Sand, gravel, ladders and vines draw as "?" on the map
The map drawing has no time budget
elements.evidence: Run in real clients on 2026-08-26, 08-31 and 09-02; the same 245-step route came back bit-identical each time.

elements.name: Block reading check
elements.summary: The dump from each game version is committed, and a test fails if the two versions name the same blocks differently.
facts: Writes continuo-block-dump.txt in the game folder
A human builds the same 32-block row in both versions
27 of 32 rows are compared across versions; 2 really differ (carpet, farmland) and 3 blocks exist only in 1.21.11
Each dump is also compared with a human-reviewed "golden" copy
log: Continuo: could not write the block dump
gaps: Agreement between versions is not proof the reading is right
No modded blocks were ever in the row
elements.evidence: Dumps produced in both real clients and signed off 2026-08-15.

elements.name: No world loaded
elements.summary: At the title screen or between worlds the bot receives no ticks at all.
facts: A world is "loaded" when both a level and a player exist
Queued K presses are discarded here
elements.evidence: Title-screen and quit-to-title steps passed on both versions (2026-08-13 to 08-15); also covered offline by the conformance tests.

elements.name: Crashed, sitting out
elements.summary: After the bot code throws, its keys are released and it gets no more ticks until the next world load.
facts: The error is logged with a stack trace
The game itself keeps running
K presses are discarded while sitting out
log: Continuo core faulted; no further ticks until the next world load
Continuo fault cleared by world load
gaps: Never exercised in a real game: it needs a deliberate crash
elements.evidence: Asserted offline by the conformance tests; the repo says no manual step can reach it.

elements.name: Guards every tick
elements.summary: One shared gatekeeper decides, each tick, whether the bot may run: only inside a loaded world, never after a crash, and never across a world change.
facts: Same code for both game versions
Watches the world object itself; a new one means "stop"
Wraps every call into the bot so an error cannot reach the game
Starts the bot exactly once per game session
On 1.21.11 it also stops the bot when the game closes; 1.7.10 has no such hook
elements.evidence: World-change behaviour seen in game on both versions (portal and quit steps, 2026-08-13); crash handling is tests only.

elements.name: Idle
elements.summary: No route and no search: the bot does nothing and writes no keys, so it never fights your keyboard.
facts: Writes nothing, not even a key release
Every stop and every world change lands here

elements.name: Searching
elements.summary: No route yet, one search running: the player stands still while the bot works through a slice of the search each tick.
facts: Used for the first search and for every retry
Always searches from where the player stands now
The measured 245-step route took about 13 ticks (0.65 s) to find
Gap jumps are not allowed in a real walk
elements.evidence: The search itself was run in real clients through the route test; the walker driving it is tests only.

elements.name: Walking
elements.summary: A route and no search: each tick the bot works out where it is on the route and states the keys that follow from that.
facts: Remembers nothing about last tick; recomputes everything
A screen opening costs one tick, then it carries on
Walks only: never sprints, sneaks or strafes
gaps: Never recorded as run in a real game
All seven of its tuning numbers are extrapolated
elements.evidence: 65 automated tests against a pretend player. The checklist says steps 13 to 22, which cover the walker, "have never been run".

elements.name: Walking and planning
elements.summary: A route and a search at once: the player keeps walking while a second search extends the route from its far end.
facts: Only happens when the route stops short of the goal
That means the search ran out of budget part-way
Trouble here cancels the planning and searches afresh
gaps: Never recorded as run in a real game
The checklist expects this on any 100-block walk; in code it needs a search that gave up part-way

elements.name: Remembers the marked goal
elements.summary: Holds the one block marked with H until K asks for it or the world changes.
facts: Lives inside the developer route-test tool
Cleared on any world or dimension change
gaps: On the one tick a world change shows up, a queued K can still read the old mark
A real "goto x y z" command is planned, not built

elements.name: Hears your K press
elements.summary: Each tick, takes queued K presses and turns each one into "walk to the mark".

elements.name: Copies terrain as it reads
elements.summary: Every block the search looks at is kept in a private copy, so each spot is asked of the game only once.
facts: A search reads each spot 4 to 16 times; the copy makes that one
Stored in small 4×4×4 cubes
A fresh copy per search; never refreshed while searching
gaps: A chunk cache was drafted but not built
The route is never re-checked against the live world
elements.evidence: Measured in game 2026-08-31: 145,076 spots served 1,842,387 reads.

elements.name: Names each block's shape
elements.summary: Turns the raw facts the game reports about a block into one of nine shapes plus fluid and tags, the same way on both versions.
facts: Shapes: air, full, bottom slab, top slab, thin layer, stair, fence, partial, unknown
Shape comes from the collision boxes, not from the block name
A small table per version adds what geometry cannot say (lava is harmful, soul sand is slow)
Each distinct block state is named once per world
gaps: "Slow", "falling" and "climbable" are worked out but nothing uses them
Ice counts as plain stone; slipperiness is not modelled
Powder snow, berry bushes, bubble columns and lily pads were never checked
elements.evidence: Both real clients agreed on 27 of 27 compared blocks (2026-08-15).

elements.name: Decides where feet fit
elements.summary: The one place that says what can be walked through and what can be stood on.
facts: Standing needs two clear blocks above a floor
Carpet and snow layers are walked through
Fences, fluids and harmful blocks are never a floor
Bottom slabs are neither a floor nor passable
gaps: No swimming and no ladder climbing

elements.name: Tries four kinds of step
elements.summary: From each spot the search asks four step types where they could take the player next: walk, diagonal, step up, drop down.
facts: Step up: one block, needs head room
Drop: lands on the first floor, up to 3 blocks down
Diagonal: both corners must be clear
New step types plug in without touching the search
gaps: Which steps a game version or the player supports is not negotiated; only a caller switch exists

elements.name: Gap jumps: test only
elements.summary: A fifth step type, a sprint-jump over a one-block gap, is found by the route test but never used or walked by the bot.
facts: Ships as a separate plug-in module
The walker searches with it switched off
If handed such a step, the walker stops
gaps: Walking it needs sprint, jump timing and velocity, none built

elements.name: Keeps the cheapest route
elements.summary: An A* search over block positions that returns the route costing the fewest game ticks to one exact block.
facts: Cost is time: walking 3.56 ticks, climbing 6.56, dropping 8.2 to 12
Stops after examining 25,000 spots
Identical world, identical route, every time
gaps: Costs assume sprinting, but the walker never sprints
Costs were derived from game source and never timed
A "any height at this X,Z" goal exists but nothing uses it
No turn penalty
elements.evidence: The same 245-step route returned bit-identical in real clients across three refactors.

elements.name: Settles for part-way
elements.summary: When the budget runs out, the search keeps the route to the spot nearest the goal and searches on from there.
facts: Only if that spot is at least 4 blocks closer
Repeats until the goal, a dead end, or no progress
A safety net; it fails below about 70% of the needed budget
elements.evidence: In-game run 2026-08-31 returned FOUND in 2 segments, identical to the earlier runs of that route.

elements.name: Spreads work over ticks
elements.summary: A search is cut into slices of 2,000 spots, one per tick, so the game never freezes while the bot thinks.
facts: Sliced and unsliced searches give the same answer
Worst slice measured: 22 ms cold, 6 to 9 ms warm, of a 50 ms tick
Runs on the game thread; a background thread was rejected

elements.name: Finds itself on the route
elements.summary: Each tick, picks the route step nearest the player, looking only a few steps either side of last tick’s answer.
facts: The narrow window stops it skipping a loop of a spiral staircase
A knock back simply moves the answer back
gaps: The window size was reasoned from an uncounted staircase

elements.name: Faces the next step
elements.summary: Aims the view at the centre of the block the current step ends on; pitch is left alone.
facts: Diagonals are walked by facing them, not strafing

elements.name: Holds Forward, jumps on climbs
elements.summary: States all seven keys every tick: Forward down, Jump down only on a step up while on the ground, everything else up.
facts: Jump is released in the air so the next jump is not throttled
Past the last step it keeps walking at the final block
gaps: Sprint is always off, though route costs assume sprint
Whether "on ground" behaves the same on both versions is unchecked

elements.name: Turns gently, not instantly
elements.summary: Limits how far the view may turn in one tick, starting from where the player really faces now.
facts: A full about-turn takes 6 ticks (0.3 s)
The intended place to add human-like behaviour later
gaps: Only turning is softened; key presses are passed straight through

elements.name: Notices it was moved
elements.summary: If the player is too far from every nearby route step (a teleport, a long fall) the route is abandoned.
facts: Nothing tells the bot it was moved; it just looks
This replaced a planned "server corrected you" signal
gaps: Whether looking is enough is the main open question for the in-game run

elements.name: Notices no progress
elements.summary: Counts ticks in which the player got no further along the route; too many and the route is abandoned.
facts: Measures progress along the route, not speed

elements.name: Searches from route's end
elements.summary: Starts a new search from the last block of the current route toward the goal, without stopping the walk.

elements.name: Joins the new part on
elements.summary: Appends the continuation to the far end of the route, so the player’s place on it is untouched.
facts: The continuation must start exactly where the route ends

elements.name: Arrived
elements.summary: The player is on the final block and that block is the goal: every key is released once.

elements.name: Refuses an unwalkable step
elements.summary: If the next step is a gap jump or has no known type, the bot stops rather than guess.
facts: Cannot happen from the bot’s own searches today
log: Continuo executor: stopping at <pos> -- a parkour step, which this executor does not grant or execute

elements.name: No route exists
elements.summary: Everything reachable was examined and the goal was not there; the bot stops and does not retry.
facts: Any part-way route already found is thrown away
log: Continuo executor: no path to the goal -- stopping rather than retrying a goal already proven impossible

elements.name: Budget spent, nothing found
elements.summary: The search hit its limit without getting usefully closer; a route may exist but the bot stops.
gaps: No automated test reaches this
The checklist calls it near-unreachable and wants it reported if seen
log: Continuo executor: search exceeded its budget with nothing to show for it -- stopping

elements.name: Gave up after 3 retries
elements.summary: A fourth retry in a row without any progress along a route ends the walk with every key released.
facts: Any progress resets the count
log: Continuo executor: giving up after 3 repaths without progress

elements.name: Sends 20 ticks a second
elements.summary: The game calls in at the start and the end of every tick; that heartbeat is the only thing that makes the bot run.
facts: The start-of-tick call is meant to land before the game reads the keys
The end-of-tick call is delivered but ignored by the bot

elements.name: Describes any block
elements.summary: Answers six raw facts about the block at a position: its id, state, collision boxes, fluid, climbable, falls.
facts: Raw facts only; the meaning is decided on the bot side
Unloaded or out-of-range positions come back "unreadable"
gaps: On 1.7.10, block boxes lose precision about a million blocks from the origin

elements.name: Names its version
elements.summary: Reports the game version and mod loader, used to pick the block table and for the startup log line.
gaps: Carries no list of what the version can do

elements.name: Reports the player
elements.summary: Gives the player’s position (feet), facing and whether it is on the ground.
facts: On 1.7.10 "y" is taken from the bottom of the body box, not the eye height
gaps: No velocity, health, inventory or "in water"
elements.evidence: Checked in game 2026-09-02: reported position matched F3 on both versions.

elements.name: Presses keys, turns view
elements.summary: The only way the bot affects the game: hold or release one of seven movement keys, and set where the player looks.
facts: Keys: forward, back, left, right, jump, sneak, sprint
The game may clear held keys at any time (any screen opening)
Works even if you unbind the key in Controls
gaps: No clicking, block breaking, item use or hotbar

elements.name: Minecraft 1.21.11
elements.summary: The translator for modern Minecraft: wiring only, it holds no decisions.
facts: Built with Fabric Loom
Also stops the bot when the game closes
gaps: No automated tests; only the manual checklist

elements.name: Minecraft 1.7.10
elements.summary: The translator for 2014-era Minecraft, running the very same bot code.
facts: Built with RetroFuturaGradle
Needs a small access patch to press keys
Has no "game is closing" event, so that stop is skipped
gaps: No automated tests; only the manual checklist
Never run "gradlew clean": it deletes the decompiled game source used for review

elements.name: Pretend game
elements.summary: A stand-in game with a scripted world and player, so the bot and the gatekeeper can be tested with no Minecraft.
facts: 28 conformance tests any gatekeeper must pass
About 590 automated tests in the repo overall
Five recorded real-terrain worlds for route tests

elements.name: More versions
elements.summary: Further versions and loaders (NeoForge, 1.20.x) are planned; each should need only a new translator.

elements.name: World changed?
elements.summary: If the world object differs from last tick the bot is stopped first; a crash flag is cleared by a world load.

elements.name: Your K press
elements.summary: Queued K presses are handed to the bot inside a world, and thrown away outside one or after a crash.

elements.name: Search one slice
elements.summary: A running search examines up to 2,000 more spots.

elements.name: Take a finished route
elements.summary: A search that just finished is adopted in the same tick: replacing the route, or joined onto its end.

elements.name: Where am I?
elements.summary: Finds the nearest route step to the player; too far from all of them means off route.

elements.name: Arrived?
elements.summary: On the last step, close enough, and that step is the goal: stop.

elements.name: Stuck?
elements.summary: No progress along the route for too many ticks in a row: search again.

elements.name: Route running out?
elements.summary: Few steps left and the route stops short of the goal: start planning ahead.

elements.name: State all 7 keys
elements.summary: Writes the full set of seven keys, whether or not anything changed since last tick.

elements.name: Turn toward next step
elements.summary: Asks for the new facing; the turn limiter caps how far the view moves this tick.

elements.name: H, L, J handled
elements.summary: After the game has moved the player: mark a goal, advance a route test by one slice, write a dump.
facts: These keys bypass the gatekeeper; each has its own error catch

elements.name: End-of-tick call
elements.summary: The gatekeeper delivers an end-of-tick call, paired with the start one, but the bot ignores it.
gaps: Nothing acts on it yet

elements.name: Bot walks forward
elements.summary: A first bot on Minecraft 1.21.11 that held Forward for 40 ticks, driven by code that knows no Minecraft.
facts: That demo walk has since been replaced by the route walker

elements.name: Same bot on 1.7.10
elements.summary: The unmodified bot code runs on a game fifteen years older, behind a shared gatekeeper with a conformance test suite.

elements.name: Understands blocks
elements.summary: Both versions report raw block facts and one shared rule set names them.

elements.name: Finds routes
elements.summary: Route search with pluggable step types, part-way fallback, a terrain copy and tick-sized slices.
facts: Merged in stages, 2026-08-17 to 09-01
gaps: Negotiating abilities with the game version was not built
The roadmap text does not mark this milestone done

elements.name: Walks a found route
elements.summary: The bot can see and steer the player and walk a found route; goals, a task manager and a "goto" command are not built.
facts: Part 1, seeing and pointing the player: merged 2026-09-02, verified in game
Part 2, the route walker: merged 2026-09-04
Part 3, goals, task manager, goto: not started
gaps: Part 2’s in-game checklist (steps 13 to 22) has no recorded run
The translator-code audit set for this milestone waits on part 3

elements.name: Remote control link
elements.summary: Planned: a local network link so an outside program can set goals, watch the search and change settings.

elements.name: Browser control panel
elements.summary: Planned, in a separate repository: drive and watch the bot from a web page.

elements.name: Mining and building
elements.summary: Planned: scripts on top of route walking, such as mining a vein or building from a schematic.
facts: The roadmap calls this point "the product"

elements.name: More game versions
elements.summary: Planned: third and fourth translators, each a re-test of the boundary.

elements.name: Flying, modded moves
elements.summary: Planned: elytra flight and mod-specific movement, with the search tracking extra state such as charge.

elements.name: Bot errors never crash game
elements.summary: Whatever the bot code throws is caught, logged, and followed by releasing its keys; the game’s own tick never sees it.

elements.name: Idle bot touches no keys
elements.summary: When not walking, the bot writes nothing at all, so it cannot fight your own keyboard.
facts: While searching with no route it also writes nothing, after one release

elements.name: All seven keys, every tick
elements.summary: While walking, the bot states its whole wanted key set and facing each tick and never relies on an earlier press still holding.
elements.evidence: With the earlier demo walk, opening the inventory mid-walk no longer stopped the player (2026-09-02, both versions).

elements.name: World change always stops it
elements.summary: Leaving, joining or switching dimension stops the bot and releases its keys, on both versions, by one shared check.

elements.name: Everything on the game thread
elements.summary: Every call between bot and game happens on the game’s main thread and may not block; this is why searches are sliced.
facts: Stated as unfalsifiable by a test

elements.name: Bot core knows no Minecraft
elements.summary: The build fails if any bot-side module mentions Minecraft, Fabric or Forge in its code or dependencies.

elements.name: Bot core stays Java 8
elements.summary: The build fails if bot-side code compiles to anything newer than Java 8, because 1.7.10 must load the same jar.

elements.name: Parts depend one way
elements.summary: A single allow-list says which module may use which; nothing may depend on a translator. Breaking it fails the build.

elements.name: Translators decide nothing
elements.summary: A translator may only rename and guard; any real decision belongs on the bot side. Checked by reading, not by a machine.
facts: Last audit, 2026-08-15, read the two block readers: 14 conditionals, none about block identity
gaps: The next audit is tied to the unbuilt third part of milestone 5

elements.name: Both versions see same blocks
elements.summary: The committed block dumps from the two games must match each other and their reviewed golden copies.

elements.name: Same world, same route
elements.summary: Limits are counted in spots examined, never in milliseconds, and ties break in a fixed order, so tests can assert the exact route.

elements.name: Distance guess never overshoots
elements.summary: The search’s estimate of remaining cost is always a lower bound, which is what makes the returned route the cheapest; every step type’s claim is audited.

elements.name: Every step has one name
elements.summary: A step’s type is worked out from where it goes; a test fails if a new step type would make that ambiguous.

elements.name: Unreadable block means wall
elements.summary: A block that cannot be read (unloaded, out of range) is never walked through and never stood on.

elements.name: Never routes through water, lava
elements.summary: Any fluid block and any block tagged harmful is neither passable nor a floor.

elements.name: Default key bindings
elements.summary: Defaults set in each translator; rebind them in the game’s Controls screen under "Continuo".

elements.name: Route map size
elements.summary: The text map is cut to 64 blocks per axis around the start, with 2 blocks of padding.

elements.name: Per-version block table
elements.summary: Nine rows for 1.21.11 and eight for 1.7.10 mark blocks as fluid, harmful or slow. Add a row to make the bot avoid a block.
facts: Unknown names in the file fail loudly at startup

elements.name: Walk-through height
elements.summary: A block whose collision reaches no higher than a quarter block can be walked through.

elements.name: Floor height range
elements.summary: A block is a floor if its top is between 0.9 and 1.0 of a block; 0.9 admits modern farmland.

elements.name: Deepest drop taken
elements.summary: The largest fall without damage, read from both versions’ game source.

elements.name: Gap jumps switch
elements.summary: The walker searches with no abilities granted; the route test grants gap jumps. Turning it on for walks is not enough: the walker still refuses the step.

elements.name: Step costs, in ticks
elements.summary: Walk 3.5636, diagonal 5.0397, step up 6.5582, drops add 4.61 / 6.79 / 8.47. Derived from game physics at sprint speed.
facts: The code says: self-consistent, "not validated"

elements.name: Search limit
elements.summary: How many positions one search may examine. Set from five recorded real routes; the hardest needed 17,423.

elements.name: Part-way must gain
elements.summary: A part-way route counts only if it ends this much closer to the goal. Swept in tests: 1 to 8 tie, 16 breaks.

elements.name: Work per tick
elements.summary: Spots examined per tick. Measured in game: halved from 4,000 after a 35.6 ms first slice.

elements.name: Look-along window
elements.summary: How many route steps either side of the last position are considered. Too large skips a staircase loop.
facts: Checklist step 22 is meant to measure or observe this; no run is recorded

elements.name: Turn speed
elements.summary: The most the view may turn per tick. Extrapolated, not yet observed.
facts: Checklist step 17 is meant to measure or observe this; no run is recorded

elements.name: Off-route distance
elements.summary: Further than this from every nearby route step counts as off the route. Extrapolated.
facts: Checklist steps 13 and 16 are meant to measure or observe this; no run is recorded

elements.name: Stuck patience
elements.summary: Two seconds without progress along the route triggers a new search. Extrapolated.
facts: Checklist step 19 is meant to measure or observe this; no run is recorded

elements.name: Arrival distance
elements.summary: How close to the final block counts as arrived. Extrapolated.
facts: Checklist steps 5, 6, 13 and 14 are meant to measure or observe this; no run is recorded

elements.name: Retries before giving up
elements.summary: Searches in a row without progress before the walk is abandoned. Extrapolated.
facts: Checklist step 20 is meant to measure or observe this; no run is recorded

elements.name: Plan-ahead distance
elements.summary: Steps left on the route when planning ahead starts. Extrapolated.
facts: Checklist step 21 is meant to measure or observe this; no run is recorded

links.label: K pressed
links.summary: With a goal marked, K stops anything in progress and starts a search from where the player stands.

links.label: route found
links.summary: The finished search’s route, whole or part-way, becomes the route being walked, in the same tick.

links.label: route nearly used up
links.summary: Few steps remain and the route ends short of the goal, so a search from the route’s end begins.

links.label: new part joined
links.summary: The continuation is appended and the walk carries on without a pause.

links.label: off route or stuck
links.summary: The route is dropped, every key is released once, and a new search starts from the player; the retry count goes up.

links.label: off route or stuck
links.summary: Same as from plain walking, and the planning search in flight is cancelled.

links.label: search ends badly
links.summary: No route, an empty-handed budget, or too many retries all end the walk.

links.label: walk ends
links.summary: Arrival, or a step the bot will not walk, ends the walk and releases every key once.

links.label: no route onward
links.summary: If planning ahead proves the goal unreachable, the walk stops at once. Not drawn on the picture.

links.label: K with nothing marked
links.summary: K with no goal marked only logs a hint.
log: Continuo: no goal marked -- stand on the destination and press the mark key

links.label: K again: start over
links.summary: K during a walk or search abandons it, releases the keys, and searches toward the current mark.

links.label: world changes: stop
links.summary: A new or missing world object stops the bot, cancels any search and forgets the block names it learned.

links.label: bot code throws
links.summary: Any error inside the bot is caught; the bot is stopped and benched.
log: Continuo core faulted; no further ticks until the next world load

links.label: next world load
links.summary: Loading a world clears the crash flag before the bot is stopped afresh.
log: Continuo fault cleared by world load

links.label: world loads
links.summary: Once a world and a player exist, ticks start flowing and the bot is idle.

links.label: world unloads
links.summary: Quitting to the title screen or disconnecting stops the bot and ends the ticks.

links.label: tick start, tick end
links.summary: The heartbeat: two calls per game tick.

links.label: raw block facts
links.summary: Collision boxes, fluid, climbable and falling flags for one position.

links.label: game version
links.summary: Chooses which block table is loaded.

links.label: position, facing, on ground
links.summary: Read fresh every tick; also gives a search its starting block.

links.label: seven keys and a facing
links.summary: Written before the game reads its input for the tick.

links.label: goal block
links.summary: H stores the block under your feet.

links.label: walk request
links.summary: K is queued by the game and collected at the next tick start.

links.label: start a route test
links.summary: L starts a sliced search toward the mark.

links.label: dump 32 blocks
links.summary: J writes the row of blocks east of you.

links.label: goal block
links.summary: The marked block is what every search aims for.

routes.name: Walk to a marked spot
stepNotes: Stand on the destination and press H
The block under your feet is remembered
Walk away, then press K
The log names the block it will walk to
The player stands still for about half a second
The cheapest route in ticks is found
The route is adopted the tick it is ready
Forward is held; the view turns step by step
On the marked block: keys released
The bot goes quiet again

routes.name: You open the inventory
stepNotes: The bot is walking a route
Opening any screen makes the game drop held keys
Next tick the bot states all seven keys again
So the walk loses one tick, not the rest of the route

routes.name: Teleported mid-walk
stepNotes: The bot is walking a route
Suddenly no nearby route step is within 2 blocks
Keys released; the log says "off path, repathing"
A new search starts from where the player now is
A fresh route replaces the old one
The walk resumes

routes.name: Something blocks the way
stepNotes: The player pushes against an obstacle
40 ticks pass with no progress along the route
The log says "stuck, repathing"
The new search reads the terrain afresh and sees the obstacle
A route around it is adopted
The walk resumes

routes.name: Knocked off again and again
stepNotes: The bot is walking
Off route: retry 1
Each new search starts before any progress is made
The fourth retry in a row is refused
Every key is up; the player must not drift

routes.name: The goal can't be reached
stepNotes: K is pressed toward a sealed-off mark
Everything reachable is examined
The goal is not among it: stop, no retry
The bot goes quiet

routes.name: Goal beyond the search budget
stepNotes: A segment runs out of its 25,000 spots
It keeps the route to the nearest useful spot
A route that stops short of the goal is adopted
The player walks it
20 steps from its end, planning starts
Walking continues while the next search runs
The continuation is appended
No pause at the join

routes.name: You leave the world mid-walk
stepNotes: The bot is walking
At tick start the world object has changed
The bot is stopped and its keys released
At the title screen no ticks arrive
Rejoining starts idle; nothing is stuck down
The old mark is gone too

routes.name: The bot code crashes
stepNotes: Every call into the bot is wrapped
An error is caught and logged with its trace
Keys released; no more ticks for the bot
The next world load clears the flag
The bot is usable again

routes.name: Test a route without walking
stepNotes: Mark the destination
Press L from somewhere else
The search runs a slice per tick, gap jumps allowed
The view turns to face the goal as a self-check
A summary is logged and a text map is written

routes.name: Check both versions agree
stepNotes: In each version, stand at the test row and press J
Raw facts for 32 blocks are read
Each is named by the shared rules
The two files are committed and compared by a test
A difference fails the build
